'''''The American Black Chamber''''' is a 1931 book by [[Herbert O. Yardley]]. The book describes the inner workings of the interwar American governmental cryptography organization called the [[Black Chamber]]. The cryptography historian [[David Kahn (writer)|David Kahn]] called the book "the most famous book on cryptology ever published."<ref>{{cite book |title=[[The Codebreakers]] |first=David |last=Kahn |author-link=David Kahn (writer) |year=1967 |page=176 |quote=Yardley, in desperation, sat down to write what was to be the most famous book on cryptology ever published.}}</ref> By describing the inner workings of the organization, the book created large interest and heightened public awareness of the United States's cryptographic abilities. In particular, the Japanese government became aware of the extent of experience that the American government had with cryptography and increased the strength of their own knowledge in cryptography in response. Reviewers suggested the book may have cost the United States significantly in the [[Pacific War]] against Japan in [[World War II]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Newton |first=David E. |title=Encyclopedia of Cryptography |year=1997 |publisher=Instructional Horizons, Inc |location=Santa Barbara California |page=12}}</ref>

The book was made into the 1935 film ''[[Rendezvous (1935 film)|Rendezvous]]'' starring [[William Powell]] and [[Rosalind Russell]].
